lesson_title: The Law of Demand at the Tuck Shop
hook_text: Drop a muffin's price from R20 to R4 and sales jump from 50 to 230. Here is why.
clip_script: At R20, 50 learners buy a muffin. At R12, 120. At R4, 230. Price down, quantity up. Price up, quantity down. That is the law of demand. Why? You switch to a vetkoek when muffins get pricey. Your pocket money stretches less far. And the third muffin is never as good as the first. Plot it: price up the side, quantity along the bottom. The dots make a slide, sloping down from left to right. Now the twist. If the tuck shop changes the muffin's price, you just slide along that line. But if a new school opens next door, more people want muffins at every price, and the whole line jumps to the right. Own price: slide. Anything else: jump. Get that right and half of price theory is done.
visual_style: Animated muffins stacking at different price tags, dots appearing on a graph to form a downward slide, then the whole curve jumping right as a second school building appears.
pacing: Quick price countdown, a steady plotting beat, a punchy slide-versus-jump finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw your own demand curve.
